entities.label: One identity per species
entities.plain: Each kind of molecule is to have one identity and one conserved total, declared once where a world is defined, however many arrays hold it: free and bound molecules of one kind are one species. Since the rework landed on 16 November 2026, a registry of species holds each species' identity, its standard chemical potential and its background in one place, so new laws need no checks against each other's species lists, and a test on main refuses any such check left in the engine. Every sum over species follows one declared order: the species are added one at a time, in the order they are declared (D182), so that raising the limit on the number of species later needs only a check on one test world and a cost measurement. Measured on the L4, this costs no measurable time at 16 species, and its sums come out bit for bit the same on the GPU and the CPU. It moved only ledgers and diagnostics, at rounding: in all 113 saved worlds every physical quantity stayed the same bit for bit. A test refuses any sum in the tissue model, the operators or the kinds that bypasses the declared order. Since the core fixes landed on 18 November 2026 an operator that declares its own standard potentials is held to the registry's: each is converted to the registry's standard concentration, and one that differs by more than rounding is refused, naming the operator (D3). Implemented and guarded. On 19 and 20 November 2026 the registry gained a check of every declared standard free-energy entry against its own sum of standard potentials, within the form's band, and, as groundwork for the mitochondria work (D234), a named potential set from Beard's published model, beard2005@1, with the moieties it requires; neither is a law, and no mitochondrion runs in the engine. A test on main holds the free-energy entries.

entities.label: Fuel as shared species
entities.plain: Decided on 15 November 2026 (D176): ATP, ADP and phosphate become ordinary species of the shared inventory. Reactions make and spend them, pumps draw from the same amounts, and the standard chemical potential of each is declared in one place. In the design, finite fuel is a transporter's default, and fuel held constant is the special case: a held row of that inventory, not a parameter of a pump. Since the rework landed on 16 November 2026, the species registry holds those standard potentials, and the transporters on main read their fuel as held rows of the inventory; finite fuel is refused there until a later step. The terms finite fuel needs in the kind interface's energy accounts landed the same evening, with the core's next lane; the transporter's own change is still to come. The first case is small: one regeneration reaction and one pump share a finite amount of fuel, and show depletion, a slower pump and recovery. Its independent reference landed on main on 15 November 2026: with regeneration stopped for 200 s, ATP falls almost to nothing and the pump to about 0.2% of its rate; two seconds after regeneration resumes the pump is back within 1%, and every account closes. Its design on the kind interface is accepted, ruled by the lead on 16 November 2026: the transporter gains a second kind of fuel that it moves, one ATP to ADP and phosphate per cycle, so fuel can run down and recover; the first world is the reference's pump of an uncharged molecule, with its store a compartment the cell owns, and the proton pump on finite fuel follows later. The engine's own case, checked against the reference, is built in step 3 of the order the user set on 16 November 2026 (D194), after one pass over the core's shared seams. Where this meets explicit proton chemistry, the boundary is declared for fuel held constant: the fuel's free energy is taken at its node's reference pH, and a stage whose pH strays beyond a declared band is refused. For finite fuel at a node whose protons change it is still open, and refused. That work booked by a reaction is not fuel is still to be declared. Finite fuel runs today only in the earlier tissue families, and the tissue model's own pumps hold their fuel constant. Designed; not on main.

entities.label: Passive routes and their laws
entities.plain: The tissue model's passive routes kind and the route laws it hosts. The first is a law for molecules that cross a membrane on their own, down their gradient: the one law added in the rework round, to show that adding a law changes nothing for worlds that do not use it. Since the rework landed on 16 November 2026 it is on main as one of the tissue model's passive routes, beside a proton leak that compartment pH uses. For an uncharged molecule its core computation is the membrane transport's own route at zero charge, and it books the heat it releases exactly, as the free energy lost by what it moved. In a closed test with two compartments it must conserve material, stop when both sides are at equal chemical potential, reverse with the driving force, and turn the free energy lost into heat with no work from outside. Its independent reference, written by a separate agent that read no engine code, landed on 15 November 2026: in it, flow and heat are exactly zero at equal concentrations, the flow reverses exactly, and heat never decreases. The engine's operator for secretion and uptake is a driven route that books work, so it does not count as passive. Implemented and guarded: on a closed pair of compartments, a test on main shows it relaxing as the independent closed form says, conserving material, and booking as heat the engine's own decrease of free energy, to rounding. It has not been judged against its own reference, and its composition with water is still a target; the passive routes ran in FR-4's and FR-5's judged acceptances on 17 November 2026, which passed, and their scope line names the compartment operator as built at 32a1d439. Until a later step, the composite model refuses an operator that writes a row such a route books exactly. The minimal-cell track's vesicle tests are its first user. On 17 November 2026 the gap-junction work found that its exact heat booking refused a step when a route's share of heat was negative by rounding alone (FR-19). It was fixed that evening: a share is refused only beyond a rounding floor scaled by its own terms, admitted shares are booked as computed, every step admitted before is bitwise unchanged, and the law keeps its identifier (D148). A band near 1 mM that the first floor left open was closed on 18 November 2026, the floor's scale now (|μ̄_in| + |μ̄_out| + 2)·|m|, and crossrev's record of the kinds was renewed at that landing, 9 of 9. On 19 and 20 November 2026 the passive routes gained two more route laws, each a general feature that real use cases found missing (D228), each cited, with its coefficients a definition's values, unsourced today, and neither judged: an instantaneous inward rectifier, its current linear in the driving force, rectified by a logistic of it and its conductance scaling as the square root of the outside potassium (D228, item 2; the Xenopus lane's first use); and the Goldman–Hodgkin–Katz constant-field flux of a charged species at its valence, read from its amounts at both ends, on membranes first (FR-15's P2). On 20 November 2026 the rectifier's square-root ratio was formed in place so that it cannot overflow (D148), a fix the Lean proofs project found. Tests on main hold the rectifier's route and the passive routes kind with both laws.

entities.label: Catalytic assemblies (GARD)
entities.plain: Development runs, not judged (D192, D197). A model family for the origin of life after the GARD model, kept only for comparison (D197): assemblies that hold counts of many kinds of molecule, exchange them with a held reservoir, catalyse one another's joining and leaving through a fixed matrix, grow, split at random, and leave lineages. The design was decided on 16 November 2026 (D192). Events are simulated exactly, one molecule at a time. Assemblies are abstract at first. The catalysis matrix is per-world data with about 100 kinds of molecule. Catalysis comes in two forms: the single-event form of a preprint's reconstruction of GARD, for the comparison, and a pair-consistent form, in which every transfer and its reverse see the same catalysts, as the engine's law. An independent check found that in a closed world of two kinds of molecule the preprint's single-event form generically fails a test of reversibility (a catalysis matrix of rank one is the exception), and that the pair-consistent form is exactly reversible. The original authors' own event rates are not established either way, and the preprint's driven runs are not affected (D192). The first experiment measures the difference between the two forms. The first comparison is with that preprint's reconstruction, three ways, approved by the user: an independent reference, that work's own test code run unchanged outside the engine, and a comparison of distributions on 40 fresh matrices at tolerances set in advance. It is a stochastic family, registered as modules, CPU only. Its first part, the general family with this law set, and its independent references merged on 17 November 2026, each a part of its own on this map, and its second part, the family's laws and operators registered, followed that evening. The comparison is still to come. On 17 November 2026 GARD's work was given the highest priority, shared with the gap-junction work, and the two are to be shown in this viewer's Experiments at the next demo (D207, amended). Implemented and guarded: GARD's law set and the family it runs on are on main with their tests, among them the kernel's check of detailed balance, which admits only the pair-consistent form as passive, and the registration of its laws and operators; the gates of both landings held, and nothing of it is qualified.

entities.plain: Landed for development, not judged (18 November 2026). The family the origin-of-life engine's first laws run on, cells.assembly_lineages@2: the second major of the assembly-lineage family. An assembly's molecules stand in places, the pool, the membrane and a lumen, and a step moves up to three molecules on each side between them; every step is reversible, under one free energy of the counts, in seconds, litres and a declared temperature. Each convention a world needs is a named token it must declare, with no default. Its ledgers book heat and work and close at every saved row to rounding, and a run repeated under the same stream identity is bitwise equal. The engine's declarations list it among the active models. The first major is frozen: version 2 edits none of its modules, reuses its folds, keys and streams, and leaves every one of its worlds bitwise unchanged. It keeps a package of its own for now (D215). It merged on 18 November 2026 with OL5's references and with a driver that runs the engine on their registered inputs. Before the verdict the lead ruled two of OL5's readings on the physics, before the builder was asked what its kernel did; under one of them the kernel had zeroed every step with an empty end state, which froze pool steps at such probe states, and it was fixed with a planted test. The references' harness first failed one row on a record rule, the ladder's stream identities repeating across rungs, though the row's physics passed; the driver was fixed with a planted test, the references were not amended, and both verdicts are kept. On the regenerated probe set the references passed 6 of 6 rows, and four planted errors applied to the engine's own records were all caught. Its landing gate held: all 113 saved worlds, tiers 1 and 2 with no changed outcome, GARD's first version bitwise unchanged, and the feature-request lane's bitwise set. Its scope: the stochastic family with general stoichiometry over places, regular mixing, catalysis on the common state and exact ledgers. Geometry, an osmotic lumen and division come in OL2 and OL3. Nothing is judged under a registered protocol, and nothing is compared with experiment. Implemented and guarded: on main with its tests in tiers 1 and 2 of the engine's test tiers.

entities.label: Origin-of-life engine
entities.plain: Cells' own engine for the origin of life, with laws from physical chemistry: catalysis that keeps detailed balance, physical assemblies and explicit sources of free energy, on the general machinery built for GARD (D197). Its first choices were decided on 17 November 2026 (D199): amphiphile assemblies first, then oligomers, then templating; selection through a finite shared pool and serial transfer; one free-energy function for every law; and two experimental anchors to be judged. The whole programme, milestones OL0 to OL9, is built in order. On the evening of 17 November 2026 the user started it (D212): its laws (OL1) and its independent references (OL5) started then, under D199, aimed at the user's first target, a simulation from first principles of lipid assemblies with lipids and chemicals going in and out, and fission: the protocell, in this viewer's words. OL1 first checked, in its design, how its laws fit the assembly family's kernel, frozen that day, without changing any of that family's worlds; OL5 wrote its reference designs in files before any engine output existed. The lead's rulings for OL1, and for the exchange, the lumen, lysis, the floor and division of OL2 and OL3, are written into the design note. It was decided the same evening that the core may change while these first experiments run, and that gates do not (D215): OL1 keeps a package of its own for now, and at OL3 one shared run loop behind the first version's invariance gate is the default. The GARD limit is exact only under the declared measure of GARD's first build (D215, amending D199). OL1 landed on 18 November 2026, for development and not judged: the assembly family's second major, cells.assembly_lineages@2, with four laws, verified 6 of 6 against OL5's references; the laws, the family and the references are each a part of their own on this map. The same day the lead ruled on the design check of OL2 and OL3, the physical assemblies and their division, and on OL5's questions for their references; those references were registered before any of their engine output, and their code comes after the second source move, which landed that day. On the evening of 18 November 2026 the user put the core and the feature requests first (D222): OL2 still lands when its gate passes, and OL3 waits for free seats and lanes. On 19 November 2026 the user resumed OL2 and OL3 at low priority, behind the core and FR-1 to FR-10 (D230). OL2's first milestone, built on a branch and not on main, holds the bilayer geometry, the exchange between phases and the permeation of membranes, for development and not yet compared with OL5's references; next, on one branch, come OL2's osmotic lumen and lysis, OL3's division of a single lineage, OL2's shared pool and serial transfer, and OL5's probe roles. entities.label: Scoped composition (door S)
entities.plain: How several operators share one field. Before the rework, one operator supplied a field and replaced all of it, so two operators that touch different cells of the same field could not be combined. Since the rework landed on 16 November 2026, an operator can declare which cells or nodes it reads and changes, whether its change adds, multiplies or replaces, and at which stage of the step; the composite model then merges the changes place by place. Two operators that change separate places must give the same result in either order, and an overlap is refused unless a rule says how to combine it. Tests on main show its acceptance: two operators on separate places give the same bits in either order, and an overlap is refused unless both changes commute. In the round, operators that close cells still change whole masks, and the one pair newly admitted is the scheduled bath beside the shared-inventory reactions; the other pairs keep their refusals. With it the chain that is its test case runs with every ledger closing: a dose in the bath, taken up into a compartment, reacting there. Since composition's first milestone, on 18 November 2026, a current read of a field that nothing changes is admitted and reads the declared value, a change at another stage is seen whatever the declared order, and only a later change at the reader's own stage is refused. Implemented and guarded, not numerically qualified.

entities.label: Gap-junction networks and tumour tissue (development)
entities.plain: Development work, not judged (D138). The record states none of this map's levels for it. Cells' own runs of the model of a public preprint made with BITSEY: J. Grodstein, J. Mathews and M. Levin, "Membrane voltage and connexin expression work together to enhance tumor growth and metastasis in cancer", bioRxiv, doi:10.64898/2026.09.02.748840, version 1, 3 September 2026, CC-BY 4.0. It asks how strongly gap junctions must couple cells for healthy tissue to turn a tumour back to the healthy state. The user gave the work the highest priority on 17 November 2026 (D207), and its driver and its note are on main since that evening. Its linear model runs as written on the engine's own pieces, the reactions operator with the passive routes' neutral law on junction routes, unqualified, and its error against dense solves falls at second order; its exact Norton-equivalent network on the tissue model's own routes is its check. The preprint's tissue tables need engine features not built yet: a charged microRNA on junctions, a two-state junction gate and larger field solves (FR-15 to FR-17). On a line of 25 cells, the first six a tumour, the driver searched for the coupling at which the tumour returns to the healthy state; an engine check first stopped that search (FR-19), and after its fix the search ran again from main, followed by a ladder of ten couplings and a 9 by 9 sheet, an extension beyond the preprint's setup. On 18 November 2026 the user answered the note's questions (D219). Its next bundle, for a free seat: the correctly specified 25 by 25 threshold case, the preprint's Figure 5a through the windowed execution and record path, and BITSEY run unmodified, out of process, for pinned reference outputs, after its licence and revision are checked; the 2D search's registration states its geometry, success criterion, horizon, bracket, refinement rule and compute budget before it runs. Two judged comparisons were approved, each under a registered protocol with code-blind references: the linear model's numerical qualification, Figure 8 judged against independently derived physical balances, with the printed recursion's discrepancy kept as a finding; and the threshold comparison, whose verdict includes successful refinement and a convergence condition declared in advance, and in which only the 2D field is a true pre-registration, since the 1D line's value was already seen. For Table 3, its logged inputs and the interventions as actually executed govern the code's target, and the printed table is kept as a separate publication target, with the mapping discrepancies reported. FR-15 to FR-17 were scheduled with the owners whose files they touch, not yet started. The same evening the user put the core and the feature requests first (D222): the bundle's steps 2 to 5 and the references for the two judged comparisons wait for free seats and lanes. On 19 November 2026 charged species in the species operators, which the work's microRNA needs, were scheduled into the core pass as a general feature, starting with a diagnosis (FR-15's F2 part; D226, D228 item 4). By 20 November 2026 its first two steps had landed as general features: charged species in the reactions operator, where every reaction conserves charge, and a charged constant-field route law on the passive routes, on membranes first; hosting it on junctions waits for two answers from the tissue model's owner. Five quick worlds of this work form a set of crossrev, recorded from the engine's source before any core change, which every later core landing must regenerate bit for bit; that holds the engine to its own earlier programs, and compares nothing with the preprint. None of this is judged.

entities.label: Lean proofs of the laws' properties
entities.plain: Not engine code: the record states none of this map's levels for it. A library of proofs in Lean, in the repository's lean/ folder since 19 November 2026, kept by a project of its own, the Lean proofs project, which commits to main from the same checkout (D227). In its own words, it connects engine laws to their proofs, numerical checks and experimental measurements, and each claim's page records its assumptions and links to the code and sources. Its index lists 32 claims about properties of the laws, such as the direction of a flux and the conservation of what it moves: 31 marked proved in Lean and one open. Of their numerical checks against the engine, 27 are marked checked and 5 failed: that inserting uncharged membrane dissipates heat that is not negative, two claims of the origin-of-life track's catalysis, the inward rectifier's, and the potassium–anion cotransport's. Its biological evidence is partial for 28 claims, mixed for one and not assessable for one, and a measurement is sought for two. Its coverage table counts direct Lean claims for 30 of the 30 registered laws and 4 of the 24 registered operators. On 19 and 20 November 2026 the record credits it with two findings fixed in the engine, the inward rectifier's square-root ratio and the K–anion cotransport's step bound, and two corrected statements of the GARD design note. The map takes none of this as a level of the engine's parts.

entities.label: Test tiers gate
entities.plain: The routine gate: every test file's outcome is compared with a recorded baseline before code lands. A file counts as changed when its exit code or its count of failures or errors differs, when its count of passing tests falls, or when its count of skipped tests rises. At D172's landing on 16 November 2026, tiers 1 and 2 (492 files) showed no changed outcome. Of tier 3's 229 files, 187 passed, and each of the other 42 was classified, none of them a defect of the round: 23 failures and 16 time-outs that were there before, two tests the round left stale, fixed in the next commit, and one that passes when run alone. The user's rule of the same day (D187) is to test as little as possible but enough for the science: each claim is proved once, at the cheapest level that can prove it, a new test must catch a planted error, and each landing's tier-3 table is frozen as the record the next run is compared with. The audit's tools merged on the evening of 16 November 2026: tier 3's table is frozen test by test, so that a later run of tier 3 is compared test by test instead of running old code again. The user approved the audit's firm list of tests to retire the same evening (D189), and the retire merged early on 17 November 2026: 11 whole files of tier 3 and 40 of tiers 1 and 2 were deleted, and 811 cases were removed from 42 more, while eight rows were held instead, each with its reason. The tiers now hold 327, 152 and 222 files, and tier 3's frozen record holds 218 files and 6,869 tests. The saving is 5.5 processor-hours per run of tier 3 and 2 minutes per gate of tiers 1 and 2. The tree before the retire is tagged, so that every retired test stays recoverable. On 19 November 2026 the user set the suite's policy on cost (D224): a fix adds a row to an existing parametrized test or nothing, a new test that compiles or runs a world states its seconds and its reason at landing, and tests no longer needed are removed in batches, each with a removal list. Tiers 1 and 2 then held 589 files, 172 processor-minutes in all. The tier record's tools gained a fold and a merge, which put a landing's measured rows onto main's record.

entities.label: Results gate
entities.plain: How the rework was accepted, and, through its comparison of saved worlds, how changes built on it are checked. A machine-readable list names every scientific result that must still hold, and the gate fails if any of them did not actually run. Every saved world is run before and after on the CPU and compared field by field (G1). At the landing, every registered protocol that uses the tissue model was also run again and had to keep its verdict (G2); the user held E07-v1's re-run, whose worlds the comparison covers instead (D181). The rework landed through it on 16 November 2026: all 113 saved worlds were the same bit for bit before the round's last change, and within its declared tolerance after it, and every registered small protocol run again passed. The comparison of saved worlds is what is in use since: it ran again at the core's next lane, at the core's fixes and on main a83d8f15, all 113 worlds the same bit for bit each time. The protocols' re-run (G2) ran at the landing and is not repeated for each lane: a lane whose comparison of saved worlds is bit for bit moves no registered result. Two parts are still owed, each shown as a part of its own: the planted changes that it must catch (G3), and the measurements of compile time, memory and run time (G4). Both run once with tier 3 of the tests on the source tree as D188's moves leave it (D194). Since 18 November 2026 a gate is sized to what a landing changes: one that changes the engine's source runs the full gate, as before: tiers 1 and 2, G1's 113 worlds, crossrev's eleven sets and the IDs; one that does not runs G1 and crossrev only where a changed file is in their harnesses' import closures, computed at the landing's head (D223). On 19 November 2026 the gate tooling moved into the repository (D220, D222): the lane check, the snapshot freeze, the feature-request lane's bitwise landing set, crossrev's set runner, which fails closed, and the fingerprint check through a move map, each tool with tests that plant failures. The same day the user amended the sizing (D229): a landing that changes no engine source runs the files of tiers 1 and 2 it can reach, found from recorded imports and file reads, an always-run set of guards and the IDs, and tiers 1 and 2 run in full each night; once the plan's fail-fast steps are in, queued heads may be gated together as a stack of two or three. The comparison's own planted-difference self-test is a test on main, and the routine test gate also flags a test file whose count of passing tests falls or whose count of skipped tests rises. On 20 November 2026 the next part of the gate tooling landed: a gate that fails fast, gates stacked over queued heads, the map of what a landing that changes no engine source can reach, a qualifier of the gates' cache, and the nightly run of tiers 1 and 2, with its timer installed.

entities.label: Ion pumps
entities.plain: The sodium–potassium pump and calcium pumps move ions uphill and spend ATP. Each is a population with a rate law. The calcium pump's comparison passed on a second protocol, after the first failed on one item. In the tissue model their fuel is held constant. Designed, not yet on main: pumps draw ATP from the same shared amounts that reactions make and spend (D176). Since the rework landed on 16 November 2026, a transporter that spends ATP to move a species across a membrane is on main, and with it the proton pump that acidifies a compartment, for feature request FR-4: both run on fuel held constant and are implemented and guarded; the proton pump ran in FR-4's judged acceptance on 17 November 2026, which passed, and its scope line names the compartment operator as built at 32a1d439.

entities.label: Fuel (ATP)
entities.plain: Pumps draw on a finite pool of ATP that has to be regenerated. That runs in the earlier tissue families; in the composite model fuel is held constant. Designed, not yet on main: ATP, ADP and phosphate become ordinary species of the shared inventory, made and spent by reactions and drawn on by pumps (D176, 15 November 2026). Since the rework landed on 16 November 2026, the transporters on main read them as held rows of that inventory, never used up. The first case of finite fuel is one regeneration reaction and one pump sharing a finite amount; it comes after FR-4 and FR-5 in the plan's order.

entities.label: Mitochondria
entities.plain: Earlier tissue families model mitochondrial ion exchange and voltage. In the modular pump tissue model, the isolated-organelle representation now includes respiration and ATP synthesis. The Engine entry gives the component evidence and the status of the whole-organelle comparison.

entities.label: Nucleus
entities.plain: The nucleus holds the cell's DNA inside a double membrane, the nuclear envelope, whose pores let molecules in and out; the nucleolus inside it is where ribosomes are put together. Nothing of it is in the engine yet: it is planned. The user decided on 16 November 2026 that Cells will model the nucleus to some extent, not down to the folding of proteins.

entities.label: Regulatory circuits
entities.plain: Small gene circuits that switch a cell between states, alone or in a bounded two-cell model of regulation and ions. A separate small model: it runs on its own, apart from the tissue models, and does not model the nucleus. It is drawn at the cell's DNA, where such circuits act. Its models are older code since the engine's first source move on 17 November 2026: the engine lists them among the older families' models, by ID only, and this map leaves their code out, since older code is kept only as a reference until the modular engine has learned from it, then dropped (D196).

entities.label: Golgi apparatus
entities.plain: The Golgi apparatus is a stack of flattened sacs where new proteins made at the endoplasmic reticulum are modified, sorted and packed into vesicles. Nothing of it is in the engine yet: it is planned. The user decided on 16 November 2026 that Cells will model the Golgi to some extent, not down to the folding of proteins. The roadmap's trafficking item leaves the Golgi's own structure out of its scope.

entities.label: Ribosomes
entities.plain: Ribosomes are the machines that make proteins, reading a messenger RNA. They lie free in the cytoplasm, often several on one messenger, and on the rough endoplasmic reticulum. Nothing of them is in the engine yet: they are planned. The user decided on 16 November 2026 that Cells will model ribosomes to some extent, not down to the folding of proteins.

syn3a.note: None of the 455 protein products of its genome carries the signature of Kv1-type potassium channels and Kv-beta subunits (IPR003972, IPR005983). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it was made from, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. It takes up potassium with a transporter instead (KtrAB, listed under extra). No ion channel of any family searched was found in this organism: its ions cross the membrane through transporters and pumps.

syn3a.note: None of the 455 protein products of its genome carries the signature of Kv1-type potassium channels and Kv-beta subunits (IPR003972, IPR005983). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it was made from, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. It takes up potassium with a transporter instead (KtrAB, listed under extra). No ion channel of any family searched was found in this organism: its ions cross the membrane through transporters and pumps.

thalecress.note: None of its 27,368 proteins carries the signature of Kv1-type potassium channels (IPR003972). The unit's human candidates carry it, so the search finds the family where it exists.

xenopus.note: 17 proteins of its 35,004 carry the signature of Kv1-type potassium channels (IPR003972): kcna1.L, kcna1.S, kcna2, kcna2.L, kcna2.S, kcna3.L, kcna3.S, kcna4.S, kcna5.L, kcna6.L and 7 more. Each is a candidate by its family alone: no source read here says which of them does the unit's work in the frog. 7 more proteins carry only the signature of Kv-beta subunits (IPR005983), which go with the machine and make none by themselves: kcnab1.L, kcnab1.S, kcnab2, kcnab2.S, kcnab3, kcnab3.S and LOC108697683. They are listed with the unit and are no candidates for its own work.

syn3a.note: None of the 455 protein products of its genome carries the signature of BK calcium-activated potassium channels, SK calcium-activated potassium channels and BK channel beta subunits (IPR047871, IPR015449, IPR003930). UniProtKB holds 4 entries of other mollicutes, the class of bacteria it was made from, that carry one of them. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. It takes up potassium with a transporter instead (KtrAB, listed under extra). No ion channel of any family searched was found in this organism: its ions cross the membrane through transporters and pumps.

thalecress.note: None of its 27,368 proteins carries the signature of BK calcium-activated potassium channels and SK calcium-activated potassium channels (IPR047871, IPR015449). The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists.

xenopus.note: 15 proteins of its 35,004 carry the signature of BK calcium-activated potassium channels and SK calcium-activated potassium channels (IPR047871, IPR015449): kcnma1, kcnn1.L, kcnn1.S, kcnn2.L, kcnn2.S, kcnn3.L, kcnn3.S, kcnn4.L, kcnt1.L, kcnt1.S and 5 more. Each is a candidate by its family alone: no source read here says which of them does the unit's work in the frog. 8 more proteins carry only the signature of BK channel beta subunits (IPR003930), which go with the machine and make none by themselves: kcnmb1.L, kcnmb1.S, kcnmb2.S, kcnmb3.S, kcnmb4.L, kcnmb4.S, LOC108716204 and LOC108717003. They are listed with the unit and are no candidates for its own work.

mpneumoniae.note: None of the 688 protein products of its genome carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it belongs to, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. Gap junctions join the neighbouring cells of a tissue, and this organism lives as single cells.

planarian.note: By their signatures, planarians have innexins and no connexins. 68 planarian gene models carry the innexin signature and none the connexin one; no UniProtKB entry of any flatworm carries the connexin signature either, while 21 reviewed human entries do. One planarian innexin has a sequence record of its own, smedinx-11. More is to be read in Abascal and Zardoya 2013, on which animals have each family, and in Oviedo and Levin 2007, on that innexin; neither states an open licence, so nothing is taken from them. Which innexins a general gap-junction law would stand for is not known.

syn3a.note: None of the 455 protein products of its genome carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it was made from, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. Gap junctions join the neighbouring cells of a tissue, and this organism lives as single cells.

thalecress.note: None of its 27,368 proteins carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. A plant's cells are joined in another way: by plasmodesmata, channels lined by the cell membrane that cross the wall between two cells (UniProt's vocabulary). 32 proteins of the catalogue are stated to be there; they stand on the cell membrane's shelf.

xenopus.note: 45 proteins of its 35,004 carry the signature of connexins (IPR000500, IPR013092): gja1, gja1.S, gja2, gja3.L, gja3.S, gja4, gja4.S, gja5.L, gja5.S, gja8.L and 35 more. Each is a candidate by its family alone: no source read here says which of them does the unit's work in the frog.

mpneumoniae.note: None of the 688 protein products of its genome carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it belongs to, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. Gap junctions join the neighbouring cells of a tissue, and this organism lives as single cells.

planarian.note: There is no connexin 45 to find in a planarian: by its signatures it has innexins, another family of gap-junction proteins, and no connexins. 68 planarian gene models carry the innexin signature and none the connexin one; no UniProtKB entry of any flatworm carries the connexin signature either, while 21 reviewed human entries do. One planarian innexin has a sequence record of its own, smedinx-11. More is to be read in Abascal and Zardoya 2013, on which animals have each family, and in Oviedo and Levin 2007, on that innexin; neither states an open licence, so nothing is taken from them. Nothing says which innexins, if any, would form a channel like this one.

syn3a.note: None of the 455 protein products of its genome carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it was made from, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. Gap junctions join the neighbouring cells of a tissue, and this organism lives as single cells.

thalecress.note: None of its 27,368 proteins carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. A plant's cells are joined in another way: by plasmodesmata, channels lined by the cell membrane that cross the wall between two cells (UniProt's vocabulary). 32 proteins of the catalogue are stated to be there; they stand on the cell membrane's shelf.

entities.label: Cx40/Cx37 heterotypic gap-junction channel

ecoli.note: None of the 4,403 proteins of its reference proteome carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). No reviewed UniProtKB entry of any bacterium carries any of the signatures asked either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. Gap junctions join the neighbouring cells of a tissue, and this organism lives as single cells.

fruitfly.note: None of its 13,814 proteins carries the signature of connexins (IPR000500, IPR013092), the family the engine's law names. 8 proteins carry that of innexins (IPR000990), the other family this machine is asked for, as on the planarian's side of the atlas: Inx2, Inx3, Inx5, Inx6, Inx7, ogre, shakB and zpg.

mpneumoniae.note: None of the 688 protein products of its genome carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it belongs to, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. Gap junctions join the neighbouring cells of a tissue, and this organism lives as single cells.

planarian.note: There is no connexin 40 or connexin 37 to find in a planarian: by its signatures it has innexins, another family of gap-junction proteins, and no connexins. 68 planarian gene models carry the innexin signature and none the connexin one; no UniProtKB entry of any flatworm carries the connexin signature either, while 21 reviewed human entries do. One planarian innexin has a sequence record of its own, smedinx-11. More is to be read in Abascal and Zardoya 2013, on which animals have each family, and in Oviedo and Levin 2007, on that innexin; neither states an open licence, so nothing is taken from them. Nothing says which innexins, if any, would form a channel like this one.

syn3a.note: None of the 455 protein products of its genome carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it was made from, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. Gap junctions join the neighbouring cells of a tissue, and this organism lives as single cells.

thalecress.note: None of its 27,368 proteins carries the signature of connexins and innexins (IPR000500, IPR013092, IPR000990). The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. A plant's cells are joined in another way: by plasmodesmata, channels lined by the cell membrane that cross the wall between two cells (UniProt's vocabulary). 32 proteins of the catalogue are stated to be there; they stand on the cell membrane's shelf.

xenopus.note: 45 proteins of its 35,004 carry the signature of connexins (IPR000500, IPR013092): gja1, gja1.S, gja2, gja3.L, gja3.S, gja4, gja4.S, gja5.L, gja5.S, gja8.L and 35 more. Each is a candidate by its family alone: no source read here says which of them does the unit's work in the frog.

ecoli.note: None of the 4,403 proteins of its reference proteome carries the signature of the sodium-potassium pump's alpha subunit, its beta subunit and its FXYD regulators (IPR005775, IPR000402, IPR000272). No reviewed UniProtKB entry of any bacterium carries any of the signatures asked either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. The wider family, the P-type ATPases, has 4 members here (copA, kdpB, mgtA and zntA), listed under extra; none carries this signature.

fruitfly.note: 2 proteins of its 13,814 carry the signature of the sodium-potassium pump's alpha subunit (IPR005775): Atpalpha and JYalpha. Each is a candidate by its family alone: no source read here says which of them does the unit's work in the fly. 6 more proteins carry only the signature of its beta subunit (IPR000402), which go with the machine and make none by themselves: Dmel\CG5250, Dmel\CG33310, JYbeta2, nrv1, nrv2 and nrv3. They are listed with the unit and are no candidates for its own work.

mpneumoniae.note: None of the 688 protein products of its genome carries the signature of the sodium-potassium pump's alpha subunit, its beta subunit and its FXYD regulators (IPR005775, IPR000402, IPR000272). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it belongs to, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. The wider family, the P-type ATPases, has one member here, annotated only as a cation-transporting ATPase (locus MPN_209, listed under extra). It does not carry the mark of the sodium-potassium pump.

planarian.note: 5 planarian gene models carry the signature of the pump's alpha subunit, and 13 carry that of its beta subunit. The alpha signature is shared with proton-potassium pumps: one further planarian protein that carries it was described as such a pump and is listed under extra instead. No planarian sequence carries the signature of the small FXYD regulators, which marks 8 reviewed human entries and no flatworm entry.

ecoli.note: None of the 4,403 proteins of its reference proteome carries the signature of the mitochondrial calcium uniporter, its regulator EMRE and its MICU regulators (IPR039055, IPR006769, IPR018782, IPR039800). planarian.note: The unit is a lumped leak of the inner mitochondrial membrane, and the only candidate the inventory names for it is the calcium uniporter. For one gene model the signature is on a shorter alternative protein of the gene, not on its longest.
